preconditions.description: The integer n is between 2 and 100 inclusive.
The input contains exactly 2n-1 lines: the first is n, followed by 2n-2 strings.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(s, str) and 1 <= len(s) <= n - 1 and s.islower() and s.isalpha() for s in input_lines[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the 2n-2 strings consists only of lowercase Latin letters and has length between 1 and n-1.

preconditions.expression: all(len([s for s in input_lines[1:] if len(s) == k]) == 2 for k in range(1, n))
preconditions.description: For every length k from 1 to n-1, there are exactly two strings of that length in the input.
It is guaranteed that the given strings are the set of all improper prefixes and suffixes of some string of length n.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout) == 2 * n - 2 and all(c in 'PS' for c in stdout)
postconditions.description: The output is a string of length 2n-2 consisting only of characters 'P' and 'S'.
The output contains exactly n-1 'P's and n-1 'S's.

postconditions.expression: any(all((candidate_string[:len(input_lines[1+i])] == input_lines[1+i] if stdout[i] == 'P' else candidate_string[-len(input_lines[1+i]):] == input_lines[1+i]) for i in range(2 * n - 2)) for candidate_string in [input_lines[1][0] + input_lines[1][-1] if n == 2 else (input_lines[1][0] + input_lines[1][-1] if len(input_lines[1]) + len(input_lines[1]) - 1 == n else '')])
postconditions.description: There exists a candidate string of length n (constructed from the two longest input strings) such that for every input string, if the output marks it as 'P', it matches the prefix of the candidate of that length, and if marked 'S', it matches the suffix of the candidate of that length.
